claim: Feeling of rightness (FOR) after a first answer predicts rethinking: low FOR gives longer rethinking and more answer changes; high FOR gives short rethinking. Sample sizes of the 2011 founder: N=60, 48, 128, 64 (abstract only). All later support so far comes from the same research tradition; no independent-lab replication found.
agent_test: Log a first-answer certainty signal; compare rethink-when-low vs always-rethink vs never at equal tokens.
audit_note: Sample sizes (60, 48, 128, 64) and the FOR effect match the 2011 abstract; the cited sources are Thompson's own tradition or secondary restatements, which the claim itself discloses.

claim: Most final answers were already the first answer: rethinking rarely changes it, and correct final answers were mostly correct at first response (74.8% base-rate, 87.6% syllogism in Bago and De Neys 2017).
agent_test: Measure how often a second pass flips a right answer to wrong vs wrong to right on our tasks.
audit_note: 74.8% and 87.6% are shares of final-correct trials on conflict problems and match Bago and De Neys; the Raoelison paper shares De Neys as author, so support is from one research network, with the Ackerman and Thompson review as a separate secondary source.

claim: Fluency is a cue for certainty and is only loosely tied to accuracy; wrong answers on conflict problems often carry high confidence.
agent_test: Check calibration of agent confidence on conflict vs no-conflict items; do not trust fast answer ease alone.
audit_note: Minor: Mata Study 1 wrong CRT confidence is 6.82 of 9 (moderately high, comparable to correct general-knowledge answers 7.11); the 85% and 91.5% figures are second-hand citations in Mata, and wrong conflict answers were still less confident than correct no-conflict answers in later studies.

claim: Many biased reasoners detect conflict: 66% lowered confidence (mean -20.8%) in Frey et al. Study 1 (N=232 biased); but 28.9% raised it. Detection is real but not universal.
agent_test: Use a conflict check (two methods disagree) as the doubt trigger and measure hit rate vs always-doubt.

claim: Conflict-detection effects on invalid inferences vanish once believability and chosen response are controlled (N=248, 2025); detection findings are sensitive to scoring.
agent_test: Score any agent doubt trigger by what the agent answered, not by item type.

claim: Giving up (opt-out) is a stable trait separate from confidence (r=.04, N=176) and tied to ability (r=.26).
agent_test: None direct; treat stop propensity as a tunable parameter, test thresholds.

claim: People use a diminishing confidence criterion: they stop when confidence passes a bar that drops over time; they may continue too long and gather unneeded information.
agent_test: Compare fixed-budget stopping vs a time-decaying confidence threshold at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: For GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 on reasoning benchmarks (GSM8K, CommonSenseQA, HotpotQA), prompted self-correction without external feedback or oracle labels does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1 -> 41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 91.5 -> 89.0), and the apparent gains in earlier work came from using oracle labels to decide when to stop; Kamoi et al. find no prior work showing successful self-correction from prompted LLMs feedback except in tasks exceptionally suited to it.
agent_test: Run a blind second pass vs none; require an external signal (tool, test, disagreement) before changing an answer.
audit_note: Numbers match Huang et al. Table 3, but 'LLM self-correction does not help' is stated for all LLMs and tasks while the evidence is GPT-3.5/GPT-4 on three reasoning benchmarks; Kamoi allows exceptions for tasks exceptionally suited to self-correction, and CRITIC without tools still gains 20.3 on TabMWP (text-davinci-003).
claim_before_audit: Without external feedback or oracle labels, LLM self-correction does not help and often hurts: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1 -> 41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 91.5 -> 89.0; oracle labels (leakage) produce the apparent gains.

claim: Finding the error is the bottleneck, not fixing it: given the mistake location, models correct well; GPT-4 mistake finding is near 53% on BIG-Bench Mistake.
agent_test: Test location-given vs blind review at equal tokens.

claim: A self-correction blind spot exists: the same error is fixed when attributed to the user but missed when attributed to the model (64.5% average over 14 non-reasoning models); appending Wait cuts it 89.3%.
agent_test: Present own earlier answer as a third-party answer before review; test against plain re-read.

claim: Verbalised LLM confidence is overconfident (mostly 80-100%, ECE above 0.377 for GPT-3, 3.5, Vicuna) and a weak failure predictor (GPT-4 AUROC 62.7%); white-box 0.605 vs black-box 0.522.
agent_test: Do not use self-stated confidence as the trigger alone; compare with sampling consistency at equal tokens.
audit_note: All three Xiong et al. entries are one paper; Kadavath et al. (2022) does not report these numbers and concerns logit-based P(True)/P(IK) confidence, not verbalised confidence, so the claim rests on a single study of 2023-era models (GPT-3, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Vicuna, LLaMA 2).

claim: Larger models are fairly calibrated on multiple-choice true/false formats and can self-rate with P(True), but calibration is poor out of distribution.
agent_test: Self-rate P(True) of own samples; check calibration on our tasks.

claim: Reasoning models express confidence better than non-reasoning twins (strictly better in 33 of 36 settings), driven by slow-thinking behaviours.
agent_test: Compare verbalised confidence calibration with and without a reasoning phase.

claim: Hidden-state probes act as a machine feeling of rightness: ROC-AUC above 0.7 everywhere, above 0.9 on AIME for 32B; ECE below 0.1; early exit saves up to 24% tokens with no accuracy loss.
agent_test: Not available for API-only agents; use a cheap proxy (trial-answer confidence, agreement).

claim: Confidence-based early exit cuts reasoning length with accuracy usually kept or improved: DEER shortens chains 19.1-80.1% on average with +0.3 to +5.0 points; Thought Calibration uses up to 60% fewer thinking tokens in-distribution and up to 20% out-of-distribution while keeping performance within a calibrated tolerance; DeepConf saves up to 84.7% of tokens online (DeepConf-low 43-79%) but accuracy drops in a few settings (e.g. Qwen3-32B BRUMO25 -0.9).
agent_test: At equal tokens compare early-exit-on-confidence vs fixed budget vs majority vote.
audit_note: Numbers match, but 'no accuracy loss' is too strong: DeepConf itself reports notable accuracy drops in a few settings (Qwen3-32B BRUMO25 -0.9, GPT-OSS-120B HMMT25 drops), and Thought Calibration preserves performance only within a calibrated risk tolerance.
claim_before_audit: Trial-answer or token-confidence early exit cuts reasoning length with no accuracy loss: DEER 19.1-80.1% shorter and +0.3 to +5.0 points; Thought Calibration up to 60% fewer tokens in-distribution, 20% out; DeepConf up to 84.7% fewer tokens.

claim: Overthinking: o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens on 2+3; the first solution round was right in over 92% of cases and used under 60% of tokens; trimming cut tokens 48.6% on MATH500 at kept accuracy.
agent_test: Stop after the first verified solution on easy items; measure tokens saved and accuracy.
audit_note: Minor: the 92% figure counts cases where a correct answer appears in the first round (conditional on an eventually correct response), not all questions; 48.6% token cut is for the authors' own self-training method on QwQ-32B-Preview.

claim: Underthinking: wrong answers use 225% more tokens and 418% more thought switches; over 70% of wrong responses contain a correct thought; a switch penalty lifts QwQ pass@1 38.3 to 44.1 on AIME24.
agent_test: Penalise early topic switching or require finishing a line before switching; test vs baseline.
audit_note: Minor: the 225%, 418%, 70% and TIP figures all come from one paper (Wang et al.; the two listed entries are the same paper); Su et al. independently confirm that wrong answers are longer. TIP 38.3 to 44.1 is averaged pass@1 on AIME2024; the 43.7 to 51.4 figure is Pass@4 with self-consistency.

claim: Longer reasoning can hurt (inverse scaling) on distractor, spurious-feature and framing tasks; on puzzles, thinking helps only at medium complexity.
agent_test: Plot accuracy vs token budget on our tasks; find where more thinking hurts.
audit_note: Minor: The Illusion of Thinking findings have been disputed in follow-up commentary; the claim reports the paper's own results.

claim: Learning when to think works: AdaptThink cuts response length 53.0% with +2.4% accuracy; a bandit meta-controller choosing continue/backtrack/switch/restart beats CoT on SciBench subsets.
agent_test: Compare a progress-report controller vs fixed policy at equal tokens (c15 numbers unverified).

claim: Humans over-trust LLM answers: default explanations produce overestimation and longer explanations raise confidence without accuracy.
agent_test: Not an agent test; relevant to output wording.

claim: Early GPT-3 models fell for CRT intuitive traps (80% intuitive vs humans 55%); ChatGPT-4 96% correct mostly via chain-of-thought; blocking chain-of-thought collapses accuracy.
agent_test: Compare with and without a visible reasoning step on trap items.

claim: Skill labels (metacognitive knowledge) given as exemplars improve math solving on GSM8K and MATH.
agent_test: Test skill-labelled exemplar retrieval; gain size not verified.

claim: Cognitive capacity predicts correct first intuition more (r=.44) than correction after deliberation (r=.22).
agent_test: Implies spending tokens on better first answers vs correction; test.

claim: Same-model critique (Self-Refine, about 20% average gain on preference-scored tasks) conflicts in spirit with the intrinsic-correction failure on verifiable reasoning; task type is the likely moderator.
agent_test: Separate style tasks from verifiable reasoning when testing review.

claim: Reflexion-style gains depend on the feedback signal's false-positive rate: with self-written tests, GPT-4 improved HumanEval Python 80 to 91 (1.4% false positives) but fell on MBPP Python 80 to 77 (16.3% false positives).
agent_test: Measure the false-positive rate of any certainty gate or self-test before trusting it as a stop signal.

claim: External or sound checks beat same-model review by a wide margin: Blocksworld GPT-4 40% (none), 55% (LLM verifier, which called 38 of 45 invalid plans valid), 88% (sound verifier); graph colouring 16% baseline, 1/100 with LLM self-verifier, about 40% with a sound verifier. On GSM8K with text-davinci-003 the tool gain over no-tool critique is small (72.2 vs 68.3).
agent_test: Use test execution or a tool as the accept test; use same-model review only as a weak extra candidate.
audit_note: Minor: Stechly et al. also find the sound-verifier gain on graph colouring comes largely from extra tries, since bare 'try again' feedback is nearly as effective as detailed feedback.

claim: Part of the apparent gain from external-verifier loops is resampling: in graph colouring the content of the feedback did not matter (binary, single-error, full-error were equal; verifier-as-stopper gave the same 40%).
agent_test: Compare any review loop against plain best-of-k at the same token count.

claim: Blind 'Wait' extension helps then hurts and loses to parallel sampling at equal tokens: R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B on GSM8K lost 11.8% going from 385 to 16,000 tokens with Wait, while parallel thinking gained 10.1%; s1-32B did gain on AIME24 (50.0 to 56.7 with Wait 4x) but with more tokens and only 30 items; removing Wait tokens cuts chains 27-51% with no utility loss (NoWait).
agent_test: At equal tokens compare gated rethink, blind Wait and k samples with majority vote; expect resampling to be the baseline to beat.

claim: Within-question ranking beats calibration as the criterion for a confidence signal: P(True) had the best within-question discrimination (62.3%) and the largest CISC saving (46% at 10 samples); verbalised binary confidence had the best ECE (0.005) but the smallest saving (10%).
agent_test: Pick a trigger signal by AUROC within the same question; the full all-signal comparison on one benchmark has not been published.

claim: Cheap black-box surfaces predict error: wrong answers are longer (MATH: over 6,000 tokens vs under 3,000 tokens for right ones); the shortest of k chains is up to 34.5% more accurate than the longest; answer agreement across samples cuts samples by 34-84% (ESC) or up to 7.9x (Adaptive-Consistency) with under 0.1% average accuracy loss.
agent_test: Use agreement and relative length across a few cheap samples as the first trigger signals; they need no logits.
audit_note: Minor: the under-0.1% average accuracy loss is reported for Adaptive-Consistency only (ESC says comparable performance); MATH length figures are from two 1.5B distilled models; 34.5% is a best-case gap.

claim: Question difficulty from the model's own pass rate predicts which test-time method works (revision for easy, parallel search for hard) and gives about 4x compute saving over best-of-N, but the published difficulty estimate costs 2048 samples per question and its cost is not charged. Models also misjudge difficulty: they overthink easy items and underthink items beyond them.
agent_test: A first short pass with agreement as the difficulty probe is untested; charge its cost in any comparison.

claim: Overthinking appears in agentic work: on SWE-bench Verified higher overthinking scores go with fewer resolved issues, reasoning models score about three times higher, and choosing the lowest-score run of 2 low-effort samples gave 27.3% at 43% less cost than o1 high effort (29.1%).
agent_test: The score is post hoc from an LLM judge; no live stop signal has been shown to transfer from math to agent loops.

claim: Thought calibration reaches up to 60% fewer thinking tokens in-distribution (s1K held-out split) and up to 20% out of distribution with performance preserved; answer-convergence stopping (Liu and Wang) cuts over 40% of tokens on NaturalQuestions with no accuracy loss, but on math benchmarks its simple answer-consistency stop can lose a lot of accuracy and the learned stop saves roughly 11-33% of tokens with small loss.
agent_test: Re-tune any stop threshold per task family; a threshold fitted on math will not carry over unchanged.
audit_note: Liu and Wang's 40% saving with no loss is on NaturalQuestions; on math (MATH-500, AIME24, GPQA) their Answer Consistency stop cuts tokens 58-87% but accuracy collapses (e.g. R1-Qwen-7B MATH-500 91.0 to 67.0), and the learned stop saves about 11-33% on math with small loss; the 60% figure is thought calibration's best in-distribution case.
claim_before_audit: Stopping on stable answers or hidden-state probes saves 40-60% of thinking tokens in math with little accuracy loss, but the saving falls out of distribution (thought calibration: 60% in-distribution, 20% out of distribution).

claim: At equal compute, sampling more solutions with majority vote beats spending tokens on generative verification until about 8x the budget; gaining 3.8% over it takes about 128x.
agent_test: Gate verification so it is only paid when agreement is low.
